title: Embedded micro-consultant scratchbook
content:
Purpose:
This is a messy personal sketch for an "embedded micro-consultant" product: a very small, transactional assistant that lives inside a host product flow (SaaS dashboard, CRM, analytics, IDE) and gives concise, actionable recommendations ("action cards") tailored to the current context. Think: 1–3 sentence analysis + one recommended action + optional quick execution (button) with telemetry.

Why this?
- Customers want contextual help that actually reduces friction (not general chat).
- Many enterprise users ask the same operational questions repeatedly (optimize config, triage alert, write short responses).
- Small surface area means easier safety/PII reasoning and faster value capture.

High-level constraints and guardrails (working assumptions):
- Micro-consultant should run on short context windows (<= 2k tokens) to keep latency <300ms when possible for hosted API.
- Default output is an "Action card" (title, 1-line rationale, recommended action, confidence score).
- Site admins can opt-in/opt-out and control whether assistant can execute actions (button).
- No raw logs of user PII left un-redacted; prefer structure outputs (codes, SKU ids) not free-form summaries saved long-term.

User problems we solve (candidate):
- "What should I do next?" for operational dashboards (alerts, root-cause hint, triage step).
- "How do I respond to this customer?" — short reply drafts for CS.
- "What's the best query/template for this dataset?" for analytics tooling.
- "Which config gives better latency/cost tradeoff?" for infra consoles.

Core flows (sketch):
1) Context capture: host app sends current view metadata + short text/context (200–800 chars) + selected entity ids.
2) Model call: Redwood API with embedded micro-consultant prompt template + policy tokens (customer-tier, region).
3) Response: structured JSON (title|rationale|action|confidence|action_payload) rendered as UI card.
4) Opt-in execution: user clicks "Run" -> host triggers API/GraphQL mutation with action_payload; Redwood records telemetry.

Example prompt template (very rough):
"You are a 2-sentence operations consultant. Given the following context (UI view + metadata + last 3 events), produce: 1) a short title (<=6 words), 2) 1-sentence rationale, 3) 1 recommended action (imperative), 4) confidence as low|med|high. Output strictly as JSON with keys: title,rationale,action,confidence,action_payload. Keep token usage minimal"

User stories (prioritized):
- As a CS agent, I want a 1-line suggested reply I can copy or send, so I can respond faster to customers.
- As a SRE, I want the assistant to suggest one triage step for a critical alert so I can reduce MTTR.
- As a PM, I want insight cards in analytics that recommend a single next query so stakeholders can iterate quickly.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- UI shows an action card under the primary toolbar for eligible views.
- Card loads within 500ms P95 for existing test orgs (best-effort for early experiments).
- 3 prebuilt templates (CS reply, alert triage, analytics suggestion) with sample prompts and unit tests.
- Admin toggle in settings + execution requires extra confirmation for destructive actions.

Privacy / Security considerations (must address early):
- Minimal context by default; DO NOT include full customer text blobs unless admin consents.
- Redaction: host should provide sanitized context layer; we ship standard redaction helpers (emails, SSNs, tokens).
- Private deployments: for on-prem customers, allow local model variants or model proxying to satisfy compliance.
- Logging: store only structured action_payload hashes + metadata; store raw outputs only with retention TTL and explicit opt-in.

Metric ideas (how we'll know it's useful):
- Activation rate: % of eligible views where user opens the card.
- Action adoption: % of cards where user clicks the recommended action (or copies the suggested reply).
- Time saved (self-reported via micro-survey) and MTTR reduction for alerts.
- False positive rate: cases where action is irrelevant (user dismiss >1s).
- Latency P95 and cost per invocation (tokens & compute).

Rollout plan (staged):
- Week 0–2: internal alpha in product team + SRE desk to get raw feedback.
- Week 3–6: invite-only beta with 3 customers (CS, infra, analytics teams). Use dedicated low-cost model variant for beta to control cost.
- Week 7–12: broader opt-in, integrate telemetry dashboards in Redwood Console (adoption, latency, cost).

Open questions / risks (notes-to-self):
- How do we quantify "confidence" reliably? Simple classifier vs prompt heuristics?
- When to include short snippets of private text vs pointers to entity IDs only?
- Execution authorization model across host product roles (who can click "Run").
- Fallback behavior if model is unavailable (show cached recommendation? show "disabled" state?).
- Cost model: charge per micro-consult call or bundle into host product route?

Experiment ideas (quick):
- A/B: card vs no-card on critical alerts -> measure MTTR.
- Template tuning: conservative vs aggressive suggestions; see adoption and reversal rate.
- Micro-survey prompt at 20% of actions: "Was this helpful?" fast toggle.

Implementation notes / engineering considerations:
- Build as a lightweight client-side component + Redwood API call. Keep UI rendering local to reduce RTT.
- Offer two modes: "suggest-only" (default) and "suggest+run" (requires host opt-in).
- Provide standardized JSON schemas for outputs so host UI can render uniformly.
- For low-latency: use short-form model variants (quantized) and cache identical context outputs for 5m.

Next steps (practical TODOs):
- Wireframe 3 card designs and share with UX for rapid feedback (Evan).
- Draft 3 prompt templates and small eval set (Sam to help build evals).
- Create JIRA spike for privacy redaction helpers (INF-2345).
- Prototype in analytics sandbox with 1 customer data view (internal pilot).

Random brainstorm fragments (leave here):
- "Action cards" could have micro-AI personas: "concise triage", "sales answer", "security auditor".
- Consider "confidence thresholds" that auto-hide suggestions below low unless user asks for them.
- Could monetize as an add-on for Dedicated/Private customers with SLA on latency.

Notes to self: keep this document lightweight. Focus MVP on 1–2 host surfaces. Avoid building a full chat UI; this is tiny, immediately useful, and easier to reason about for compliance.

-- m.s.
